## RPG

- Page: pages/papers/rpg.md
- Venue: KDD’25
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP; Inference: Graph
- TL;DR: RPG predicts long, unordered OPQ Semantic IDs in parallel with a multi-token prediction loss and decodes over a graph of valid IDs, replacing autoregressive beam search over short IDs.
- [Code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/RPG_KDD2025)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews: Sports and Outdoors, Beauty, Toys and Games, and CDs and Vinyl; filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: The four Amazon categories and chronological protocol are stated, but 5-core or other filtering rules are not stated in the body or appendix; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p2, dataset counts in https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.T1.
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-last-out: last item for test, second-last for validation, earlier items for training.
  - Source: The last interaction is test, the second-last validation, and the remaining earlier interactions form the training history; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p2.
- **Candidates**: Evaluation candidate protocol: not reported (full catalog versus sampled-negative ranking). Inference searches a graph of valid catalog items and scores only visited nodes; per-user exclusion rules are not reported.
  - Source: The evaluation description does not specify full-catalog versus sampled-negative ranking; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p2. The separate inference description builds a graph over valid catalog items and starts with b random valid nodes; this does not by itself establish the evaluation candidate protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS3.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS3.SSS2.p2.
- **Visibility**: Tokenizer exposure of test-only items: not reported. The long-tail analysis groups items by training frequency [0,5], [6,10], [11,15], and [16,20]; it does not isolate strictly unseen items from low-frequency items.
  - Source: Figure 5 combines zero-frequency and low-frequency targets, so it cannot establish separate strictly unseen-item performance; tokenizer exposure of those targets is not specified; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS5.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: Parallel OPQ subspaces, with best lengths Sports 16, Beauty 32, Toys 16, and CDs 64; per-subspace codebook size: not reported as an experimental setting. Colliding items retain separate graph nodes; no guaranteed collision-free identifier is claimed.
  - Source: Best SID lengths are in Table 6; the 256-entry codebook in the introduction is an example, not an explicit main-experiment setting; item-based graph nodes permit collisions; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#A2.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#A3.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Initial random seeds and retained beam b=10; best (neighbors k, iterations q): Sports (100,2), Beauty (100,3), Toys (50,5), CDs (500,3). One NVIDIA RTX 3090 24GB; inference batch size: not reported (training batch size is 256). Sports-only fixed-configuration scaling experiment reports approximately 15x faster inference and 25x lower runtime memory than TIGER; these are not total-storage reductions or per-request latency claims.
  - Source: Table 6 supplies b/k/q; Appendix B supplies hardware and separates checkpoint selection from graph-budget tuning; the batch size 256 in Section 3.1 is a training setting, not an inference setting; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#A2.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#A2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p6. Speed/memory scope: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS3.p2.
- **Results from**: arXiv:2506.05781v1: Table 2 (main ranking results), Table 3 (ablations), Table 4 (semantic-encoder-controlled comparison), Figure 3 (Sports efficiency), Figure 5 (training-frequency analysis), and Tables 6 and 8 (best inference budgets and memory scope).
  - Source: Overall ranking metrics, graph/architecture ablations, encoder-matched comparisons, and the bounded efficiency study are separate result locations; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.T4, and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.F3.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: RPG compares its parallel OPQ-token prediction and graph-constrained decoding with TIGER's autoregressive RQ-VAE-token generation.; where: RPG v1, Section 2.1.1 describes OPQ: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p1; Section 2.4.2 explicitly contrasts TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS4.SSS2.p1; Section 3.1 names the TIGER baseline and Table 2 compares results: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.T2.
- id: vq-rec; relation: predecessor; note: RPG follows VQ-Rec in using optimized product quantization, then predicts individual codes and searches an item graph instead of using VQ-Rec's retrieval model.; where: RPG v1, Section 2.1.1 explicitly follows Hou et al. (2023) for OPQ: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p1; Section 2.4.1 identifies the compared model as VQ-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS4.SSS1.p1; Table 2 includes VQ-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.T2.
- id: letter; relation: alternative; note: LETTER regularizes a hierarchical RQ-VAE tokenizer for collaborative alignment and code diversity, whereas RPG uses long OPQ codes with parallel prediction to improve inference efficiency.; where: Manually compared mechanisms, not a head-to-head evaluation: RPG v1, Section 4 cites LETTER (Wang et al., 2024a) among quantization methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S4.p2; Section 2.1.1 gives RPG's OPQ rationale: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p1; LETTER v1, Section 3.1 defines its regularized hierarchical RQ-VAE tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: With 64-token IDs, RPG outperforms generative baselines by an average of 12.6% on NDCG@10 and also improves inference efficiency (Abstract).
Limitation: The authors assume that the tokens of an SID are conditionally independent given the input sequence, and the decoding graph must be rebuilt when the model is retrained or items are re-tokenized (Sec. 2.2.1, Sec. 2.3.1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Generative recommenders such as TIGER decode a Semantic ID (SID) token by token with beam search, which needs several forward passes of the generator per recommendation. As a result, existing models keep SIDs short, often 4 tokens (Abstract). RPG instead predicts every token of a long, unordered SID in one forward pass and searches a graph of valid SIDs at inference. ACERec and SPRINT, later papers in the same matrix cell, use the same `Par. OPQ` tokenization and `Non-AR` backbone.

> "Running beam search for 32 steps would be computationally prohibitive." (Sec. 1)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```
Item features → semantic encoder → item embedding
  │
  ▼  OPQ: one codebook per subvector
Unordered SID (c1, ..., cm), m up to 64
  │
  ▼  token embeddings pooled per item; Transformer decoder over the history
Sequence representation s
  │
  ▼  m MLP heads, one softmax per codebook (MTP loss in training)
Cached token log-probabilities p(1), ..., p(m)
  │
  ▼  graph-constrained decoding: sample b items, add graph neighbors, keep the best b, repeat q times
Top-K items
```

#### Step 1: Long SIDs from OPQ

RPG replaces residual quantization with optimized product quantization (OPQ), so that the tokens can be predicted in parallel rather than one after another (Sec. 2.1.1).

> "To align with parallel decoding, we tokenize each item into an unordered long semantic ID (up to 64 tokens per item) using optimized product quantization (Jégou et al., 2011; Ge et al., 2014)." (Sec. 1)

OPQ splits the item's semantic embedding into $`m`$ subvectors and quantizes each subvector with its own codebook of size $`M`$ (Sec. 2.1.1). The paper cites OPQ and does not restate its rotation or codebook training. The standard product-quantization assignment is:

```math
\mathbf{x}_i = \left[\mathbf{x}_i^{(1)}; \dots; \mathbf{x}_i^{(m)}\right], \qquad c_{i,j} = \arg\min_{c \in \mathcal{C}^{(j)}} \left\| \mathbf{x}_i^{(j)} - \mathbf{a}_c^{(j)} \right\|_2^2
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{x}_i`$ is the semantic embedding of item $`i`$ after the OPQ rotation;
- $`\mathbf{x}_i^{(j)}`$ is its $`j`$-th subvector;
- $`\mathcal{C}^{(j)}`$ is the $`j`$-th codebook with $`M`$ codewords $`\mathbf{a}_c^{(j)}`$;
- $`c_{i,j}`$ is the $`j`$-th token of the SID of item $`i`$.

"Unordered" means that no token is predicted from the tokens before it. Position $`j`$ still belongs to codebook $`j`$ (Sec. 2.1.1). Different items can share the same token set. Each item keeps its own node in the decoding graph, and the authors describe such collisions as very unlikely with 64-token IDs (Appendix C).

#### Step 2: Item-Level Input

A 64-token SID per history item would make the input sequence too long (Sec. 2.1.2). RPG gives each codebook a learnable token embedding table $`\mathbf{E}_j \in \mathbb{R}^{M \times d}`$ and pools the $`m`$ token embeddings of an item into one vector $`\mathbf{v}_i = \mathrm{Aggr}(\mathbf{e}_{1,c_{i,1}}, \dots, \mathbf{e}_{m,c_{i,m}})`$ with mean or max pooling (Sec. 2.1.2). A Transformer decoder reads the sequence $`\mathbf{v}_1, \dots, \mathbf{v}_{t-1}`$ and outputs a sequence representation $`\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{R}^{d}`$ (Sec. 2.2.1).

#### Step 3: Parallel Prediction with the MTP Loss

RPG predicts each token of the next SID with its own head and trains all heads with a multi-token prediction (MTP) loss.

> "Since each token produced by OPQ encodes a separate subvector of the target item's semantic representation, we assume that tokens in the tuple are conditionally independent given the input sequence s." (Sec. 2.2.1)

```math
\mathcal{L} = -\sum_{j=1}^{m} \log \mathbb{P}^{(j)}(c_{t,j} \mid s) = -\sum_{j=1}^{m} \log \frac{\exp\left(\mathbf{e}_{c_{t,j}}^{\top} g_j(\mathbf{s}) / \tau\right)}{\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}^{(j)}} \exp\left(\mathbf{e}_{c}^{\top} g_j(\mathbf{s}) / \tau\right)}
```

where:
- $`c_{t,j}`$ is the $`j`$-th token of the target item's SID;
- $`g_j`$ is an MLP projection head for codebook $`j`$;
- $`\mathbf{e}_c`$ is the token embedding of token $`c`$;
- $`\tau`$ is a temperature (Eq. 1).

#### Step 4: Cached Token Scores

For one input sequence, RPG computes each codebook's token distribution once and caches it (Eq. 2). The score of any candidate SID is then a sum of cached values (Eq. 3):

```math
\mathbf{p}^{(j)} = \mathrm{softmax}\left(\mathbf{E}_j\, g_j(\mathbf{s}) / \tau\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{M}, \qquad \mathrm{score}(c_1, \dots, c_m) = \sum_{j=1}^{m} \log p^{(j)}_{c_j}
```

where $`p^{(j)}_{c_j}`$ is the entry of $`\mathbf{p}^{(j)}`$ for token $`c_j`$ (Sec. 2.2.2).

#### Step 5: Graph-Constrained Decoding

After training, RPG builds a graph whose nodes are the SIDs of catalog items (Sec. 2.3.1). The similarity of two SIDs is the sum of the inner products of their token embeddings:

```math
\mathrm{sim}(i, i') = \sum_{j=1}^{m} \mathbf{e}_{j,c_{i,j}}^{\top}\, \mathbf{e}_{j,c_{i',j}}
```

Each node keeps its $`k`$ most similar neighbors and an edge to itself. The graph is reused until the model is retrained or the items are re-tokenized (Sec. 2.3.1). Decoding then runs four steps (Sec. 2.3.2):

1. Sample $`b`$ SIDs from the catalog as the initial beam.
2. Add all $`b \times k`$ graph neighbors of the beam to a candidate set.
3. Score the candidates with the cached values and keep the best $`b`$.
4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for $`q`$ iterations and return the final beam as the top-$`K`$ items.

> "Since neighboring nodes in the graph tend to have similar logits, we expand the beam by propagating through the graph, including all b×k neighbors of the current beam into a temporary set." (Sec. 2.3.2)

```python
import torch

def rpg_decode(s, heads, token_emb, item_codes, neighbors, b=10, q=2, tau=0.05):
    """
    s:          [d] sequence representation of one user
    heads:      list of m projection heads g_j, each mapping [d] -> [d]
    token_emb:  [m, M, d] token embedding tables E_j
    item_codes: [N, m] SID of every catalog item; entry j indexes codebook j
    neighbors:  [N, k] graph neighbors of every item, including the item itself
    """
    m = item_codes.size(1)
    # Eq. 2: one softmax per codebook, cached for this user
    proj = torch.stack([g(s) for g in heads])                                         # [m, d]
    log_p = torch.log_softmax(torch.einsum("jcd,jd->jc", token_emb, proj) / tau, -1)  # [m, M]
    # Eq. 3 for the whole catalog; the paper scores only the visited nodes (Sec. 2.3)
    scores = log_p[torch.arange(m), item_codes].sum(dim=-1)                          # [N]
    # step 1: random initial beam of b valid SIDs
    beam = torch.randperm(item_codes.size(0))[:b]                                     # [b]
    for _ in range(q):
        # step 2: beam plus graph neighbors, without duplicates
        cand = torch.unique(neighbors[beam].reshape(-1))                              # [<= b*k]
        # step 3: keep the b best candidates
        beam = cand[torch.topk(scores[cand], k=min(b, cand.numel())).indices]
    return beam                                                                       # item indices
```

Simplifications: The code scores every item in the catalog (`scores` covers the whole catalog) before the graph search. It therefore does not implement the Sec. 2.3 path that starts from a few sampled seeds and scores only the items reached along graph edges, and it does not reproduce the paper's inference efficiency. It also takes the heads, token embeddings, and graph as inputs, and omits OPQ, the Transformer decoder, MTP training, and graph construction.

> "Compared to generative models like TIGER (Rajput et al., 2023), RPG reduces the number of sequence encoder forward passes per input instance from approximately O(bm) to just O(1), greatly improving inference efficiency (Section 3.3)." (Sec. 2.4.2)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Overall: with 64-token IDs, RPG outperforms the generative baselines by an average of 12.6% on NDCG@10 (Abstract). Table 2 gives the full comparison (Table 2).
- Efficiency: on Sports, RPG uses less runtime memory and less inference time than TIGER (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 3).

  > "Moreover, RPG reduces runtime memory consumption by nearly 25× and achieves an inference speedup of almost 15× compared to TIGER." (Sec. 3.3)

- ID length: performance does not rise with every increase in length. The best lengths are 16 on Sports, 32 on Beauty, 16 on Toys, and 64 on CDs (Sec. 3.5.1, Fig. 4).

  > "From Figure 4, we observe that, in general, longer OPQ-based semantic IDs lead to better performance. However, for smaller datasets, they may converge earlier." (Sec. 3.5.1)

- Semantic encoder: the main runs use OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, and Table 4 repeats the comparison with sentence-t5-base for parity with benchmark results (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 3.5.2).
- Long-tail items: on Sports, the authors report that RPG achieves the best overall performance across the training-frequency groups (Sec. 3.5.3, Fig. 5).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The parallel heads rest on an assumption: the tokens of an SID are conditionally independent given the input sequence (Sec. 2.2.1). The authors state that different items can share the same token set (Appendix C). They also state that the efficiency study uses one fixed set of hyperparameters, and that its runtime memory covers the GPU memory for computing logits, not the storage of model parameters (Sec. 3.3).

**Our analysis.**

- The score of an SID is a sum of per-token scores (Eq. 3), so the model cannot express dependencies between tokens of one SID. In the same cell, ACERec adds contrastive and auxiliary objectives (`MTP + Ctr. + Aux.`), and SPRINT replaces the objective with `Dual-level Flow Ctr.`; both keep `Par. OPQ` and `Non-AR`.
- The decoding graph is an index outside the model. It has one node per catalog item and must be rebuilt after retraining or re-tokenization (Sec. 2.3.1).
- The evaluation covers four Amazon datasets. The paper reports no online or industrial test.

## S2GR

- Page: pages/papers/s2gr.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: CoBa RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: Beam
- Setup card: no
- Relations: 0

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/s2gr.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### S2GR：潜空间逐步语义引导推理

> S2GR 在生成 SID 的每一步注入语义引导信号，使模型在潜空间中逐步缩小推荐候选范围。

### 研究动机与问题定义

传统生成器通常只在最终 SID 上接受监督，缺乏对中间 token 决策的细粒度引导。S2GR 研究如何利用 SID 层次结构在生成过程中表达逐步推理。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`交互图与物品内容 → 协同平衡RQ-VAE → 逐步语义引导 → 生成SID → 推荐物品`

模型先构造物品共现图并学习兼顾协同关系和码本均衡的 RQ-VAE。生成时把逐步思考 token 插入 SID 序列，并用语义引导对齐监督中间状态；完整 SID 直接确定物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户交互、物品内容和物品共现图 |
| 信息融入位置 | RQ-VAE、生成中间状态和对齐目标 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化序列，交织推理 token |
| 适用场景 | 常规和工业生成式推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 协同与均衡 RQ-VAE
S2GR 先根据物品共现构建协同图，并在 RQ-VAE 中加入码本均衡约束。量化器得到层次化 SID，同时减少 codeword 使用偏斜，为后续逐步推理提供稳定结构。

#### 4.2 逐步语义引导推理
模型把 thinking token 交织到 SID 生成过程中。每个 thinking token 对应一个层次或候选簇，生成器据此从粗粒度语义逐步缩小到细粒度 code；中间状态接受语义对齐监督。

#### 4.3 训练与部署
训练联合 next-item 生成、语义-行为对齐、码本均衡和逐步监督。推理时按层次顺序生成 thinking token 与 SID，最终完整标识直接映射到物品。论文还报告线上测试和不同规模分析。

### 实验结论

- 逐步语义引导提升了推荐效果。
- 协同平衡量化和中间状态监督均有贡献。
- 论文报告了工业线上测试结果。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 交织推理 token 增加序列长度与服务成本。
- 工业线上收益的可复现细节有限。

#### 研究定位
S2GR 的贡献是把 SID 的层次结构转化为逐步推理信号，适合放在“潜空间推理与结构化生成”章节。

### 标签

`潜空间推理` · `语义引导` · `协同量化` · `生成式推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图3。图片使用许可待核实。*

## SIDReasoner

- Page: pages/papers/sidreasoner.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: C-Beam
- Setup card: no
- Relations: 0

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/sidreasoner.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### SIDReasoner：基于语义标识推理的生成式推荐

> SIDReasoner 让语言模型在生成最终语义标识前显式推理用户偏好，以提升跨域和冷启动推荐能力。

### 研究动机与问题定义

直接预测 SID 容易把推荐当作模式匹配，难以利用物品语义和用户偏好之间的中间关系。SIDReasoner 将推理文本或结构化思考引入 SID 生成过程。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史与物品信息 → 对齐语料预训练 → 偏好推理 → 生成SID → 推荐物品`

模型以语义标识为推荐目标，先通过丰富的对齐语料学习语义、行为和标识之间的关系，再使用冷启动推理激活与分组强化学习优化推理链。最终输出 SID 直接映射物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户行为、物品语义和跨域推荐数据 |
| 信息融入位置 | 对齐语料、推理过程和强化学习奖励 |
| 语义标识结构 | 推理序列后接多 token SID |
| 适用场景 | 跨域、冷启动和常规推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 任务形式化
SIDReasoner 将推荐输出表示为语义标识，并要求模型在生成标识前形成与用户历史和物品语义相关的推理过程。推理文本和最终 SID 在同一生成任务中衔接。

#### 3.2 丰富的 SID-语言对齐
模型构造多种对齐语料，让 SID 能被翻译为物品语义、让物品内容能解释 SID，并同时学习行为序列预测。该阶段的作用是把离散标识嵌入语言模型的语义空间。

#### 3.3 推理增强强化学习
方法包含冷启动推理激活和分组强化学习。模型根据候选推理路径及最终推荐结果获得奖励，训练其生成更有依据的偏好分析，再输出目标 SID。

#### 3.4 实验与分析
论文评估跨域泛化、不同对齐策略、模型规模和强化学习设置，重点观察推理能力是否真正转化为推荐收益。

### 实验结论

- 推理增强改善了跨域推荐表现。
- 丰富对齐语料、冷启动激活和强化学习均有独立贡献。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 推理文本会增加生成长度和推理成本。
- 推理质量、奖励设计与真实用户意图之间仍可能存在偏差。

#### 研究定位
SIDReasoner 的贡献是把 SID 作为推理对象而不只是输出标签，适合放在“推理增强生成式推荐”章节。

### 标签

`语义标识推理` · `强化学习` · `跨域泛化` · `生成式推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图1。图片使用许可待核实。*

来源：`d61aa6c:tables/all-methods.md`。

- 核心贡献：在SID生成前进行偏好推理。
- 使用场景：跨域与冷启动。

## SIDScope

- Page: pages/papers/sidscope.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: n/a; Tokenization: n/a; Backbone: n/a; Tokenizer: n/a; Objective: n/a; Inference: n/a
- TL;DR: SIDScope is a diagnostic resource, not a new recommender: it checks released Semantic ID mappings for code organization, item resolution, and model compatibility after a refresh.
- [Code](https://github.com/jdding/sidscope)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Diagnostic resource with nine named exports from seven tokenizer families: Amazon Musical, Video Games, Beauty (P5), and Instruments, plus Yelp Business; eight exports enter the executable diagnostic matrix. A separate DACT Tools case studies mapping refresh. For the compact D3 graph, duplicate user-item pairs are removed and only users with 2-50 distinct mapped items are included; users above 50 are excluded, not truncated. Upstream dataset filtering is not reported uniformly across routes.
  - Source: Table 2 defines named route coverage, Section 3.2 defines bounded-graph filtering, and Section 6 adds a separate Tools lifecycle case; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.SS1.p1.
- **Split**: Protocol-dependent. Mapping profiles use declared training splits or supplied reference interactions when split labels are absent. Fixed-budget Beauty studies use explicit training/validation splits; ReSOT Instruments uses earlier events as history, the penultimate event for validation, and the final event as unused future holdout, with hashed users separating diagnostics from 2,000 validation users. GRID beam studies train outside each of two evaluation folds; DIGER uses a last-event case. DACT refresh uses the same 5,364 held-out users/targets across states, with test targets excluded from training and checkpoint selection.
  - Source: Profile, fixed-budget, beam, and lifecycle studies use distinct splits, so none is promoted to a resource-wide train/test protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS5.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.SS1.p2.
- **Candidates**: Protocol-dependent: fixed-budget prefix retrieval uses exactly 100 candidate items per user, with sensitivity budgets of 50 and 200; sampled-ranking tests use the target plus 100 catalog negatives after excluding history items, using popular or uniformly sampled negatives; frozen-beam resolver comparisons use the same top-50 generated paths, with top-20 sensitivity and no candidate-budget expansion.
  - Source: Fixed-budget retrieval, sampled ranking, and beam accounting have different candidate meanings; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS3.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS4.p2.
- **Visibility**: No single warm/cold regime. Fixed-budget studies separate diagnostic and validation users, not the upstream tokenizer's training population. The DACT refresh case includes 584 new-item targets and compares the released checkpoint with adapted checkpoints; whether these items were unseen during tokenizer fitting is not reported.
  - Source: Disjoint diagnostic users do not establish tokenizer-unseen items, and the DACT new-item handoff is not a declared tokenizer-cold-start protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.SS1.p2.
- **SID**: Named exports have 3 or 4 SID levels; a single layers-by-codebook-size configuration is n/a, and nominal per-level codebook capacities are not reported uniformly across routes. Table 3's D1 counts are occupied first-level symbols, not nominal capacities. Shared full codes are measured explicitly; frozen-beam comparisons use singleton credit, uniform within-leaf expected credit, or deterministic training-popularity resolution with item-ID tie-breaking.
  - Source: Table 2 gives SID depths, Table 3 reports occupied symbols rather than codebook capacity, and Section 5.6 defines the collision-accounting/resolution alternatives; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS6.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS6.p2.
- **Inference budget**: DACT TIGER/T5 constraint comparison: beam width 50 on 500 fixed targets. Controlled GRID/P5 GRU runs: beam width 50 on 500 targets per evaluation fold, with a DIGER portability case under the same accounting. Three GRU exports each contain 25,000 beam rows for 500 targets. Generator inference hardware, inference batch size, and latency not reported; the stated batch size 512 is for GRU training.
  - Source: Sections 5.4-5.5 state the actual beam budgets, Appendix B.4's batch 512 is a training setting, and Section 3.2 distinguishes topology from runtime; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS5.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS4.p2, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 3: eight-route D1-D5 profiles. Table 4: D3 calibration checks. Table 5: fixed-budget prefix retrieval. Section 5.4: released TIGER/T5 constrained versus unconstrained decoding. Table 6: controlled beam accounting. Table 7: resolution policies on identical beams. Table 8: DACT mapping refresh and generator handoff. Appendix B, Tables 11-12: measurement checks and candidate-budget sensitivity.
  - Source: The cited tables separate mapping diagnostics, candidate exposure, beam accounting, resolver outcomes, and lifecycle handoff; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T7, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.T8, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.T11, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.T12.

## SIIT

- Page: pages/papers/siit.md
- Venue: arXiv’24
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization

## Think2Go

- Page: pages/papers/think2go.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/think2go.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### Think2Go：带大语言模型推理的生成式下一兴趣点推荐

> Think2Go 将监督微调和强化学习推理统一到自回归生成中，通过自纠错和自适应优势校准提升 LLM 对 POI SID 的理解。

### 研究动机与问题定义

用户移动轨迹具有稀疏、周期和多步空间规律，单步生成可能难以捕获深层意图。另一方面，独立训练的 SID 对 LLM 来说只是符号序列，模型未必理解 token 的类别和空间意义。Think2Go 研究如何让生成模型在输出下一 POI SID 前进行可控推理，并保持对行为模式的记忆。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史SID/时间 → Think → Self-Correct → Answer SID`

Think2Go 在一个自回归框架中同时训练推理轨迹和最终答案。监督微调先教模型生成思考与 SID，强化学习再用答案奖励更新推理过程；Prompt epistemic uncertainty（提示认知不确定性）鼓励难例探索，reward-informed advantage scaling（奖励感知优势缩放）调节不同难度样本的更新幅度。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户历史 SID、时间信息和 POI 生成结果 |
| 信息融入位置 | 推理提示、答案监督和奖励校准 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 下一 POI、跨域泛化和推理增强推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 模型架构
模型接收带时间的用户历史和目标上下文，输出 reasoning、Self-Correct 和 Answer 三类 token。Answer 是最终 POI SID，reasoning 用于表达用户偏好和时空判断，Self-Correct 连接推理阶段与监督答案阶段。

#### 4.2 自适应优势校准
作者指出只用普通优势估计可能造成不同难度样本更新幅度相同，或因估计偏差抑制探索。Think2Go 用核密度估计当前提示与用户历史的时空周期匹配程度，得到提示认知不确定性，并据此调节优势权重。

#### 4.2.2 奖励感知缩放
奖励被相对于同组样本最大值归一化，用于缩放策略梯度。高价值且难度合适的样本得到更有效更新，减少噪声奖励导致的过拟合和策略熵塌缩。

#### 4.2.3 规则奖励与训练目标
规则奖励综合答案 SID 正确性、格式合法性和时空行为匹配。模型在自回归推理轨迹上计算奖励，并用校准后的策略优化目标更新；这种设计形成隐式课程学习。

#### 附录：自纠错与零样本 SID 语义预测
附录给出 Self-Correct 提示格式和零样本类别预测任务。模型在答案错误时生成修正建议；类别预测实验用于检查微调和强化学习后，SID 是否承载可恢复的语义信息。

### 实验结论

- 三个真实数据集上的实验显示 Think2Go 能提升生成式下一 POI 推荐效果和 SID 语义理解。
- 优势校准、推理轨迹和自纠错的消融支持其对探索与训练稳定性的贡献。
- 相比基于完整文本提示的推理方法，论文报告 Think2Go 在训练时间、测试时间和显存占用上更高效。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- 推理轨迹增加输出长度和推理成本，效果与效率之间需要按场景权衡。
- 规则奖励和核密度不确定性估计依赖数据分布，跨城市和极少行为用户的可靠性仍需验证。

#### 研究定位

Think2Go 适合放在“推理增强的语义标识生成推荐”章节，重点体现将 SID 理解、显式推理和自适应强化学习结合起来。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28997)

### 标签

`下一兴趣点推荐` · `推理增强` · `强化学习` · `自纠错`

## TIGER

- Page: pages/papers/tiger.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’23
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: TIGER encodes item text into RQ-VAE Semantic IDs and trains a Transformer encoder-decoder to decode the next item's ID, instead of retrieving items by approximate nearest neighbor search.
- [Code (third-party)](https://github.com/baiyimeng/TIGER)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews (May 1996-July 2014): Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games. Users with fewer than 5 reviews are filtered; an item-frequency filter is not reported. Retained item counts: 12,101 / 18,357 / 11,924, respectively.
  - Source: Dataset/date range and user-only filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1; corpus sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.T6.
- **Split**: Chronological per-user leave-one-out: last interaction for test, penultimate for validation, earlier interactions for training; training histories contain at most 20 items. Separate Beauty cold-start experiment: remove 5% of test items from the training split.
  - Source: Chronological ordering, exact leave-one-out allocation, and training-history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1. The separate Beauty cold-start manipulation removes 5% of test items from the training split: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p3.
- **Candidates**: Main evaluation: full catalog versus sampled candidates not reported. Cold-start retrieval adds unseen items sharing the first three codes with a generated SID to the matching seen item; epsilon caps the proportion of unseen items in the returned top-K list (epsilon=0.1 in Fig. 5a).
  - Source: Full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation is not specified in Methods/Experiments or Appendices A-E; the evaluation description is https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1. Cold-start candidate construction and unseen-item quota: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p4; epsilon=0.1 comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p5.
- **Visibility**: Main leave-one-out evaluation: per-target generator/tokenizer training visibility not reported. Beauty cold-start experiment: unseen by tokenizer too; the selected items are removed from the training split, both RQ-VAE and the generator are trained on that split, and unseen-item SIDs are produced afterward.
  - Source: Main preprocessing defines interaction holdouts without explicitly enumerating item-level training visibility: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4. For the cold-start experiment both RQ-VAE and the sequence-to-sequence model are trained on the reduced training split; unseen items are encoded afterward: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p3.
- **SID**: Main configuration: 3 residual-quantization levels x 256 codewords (32-dimensional code embeddings), plus a fourth collision-disambiguation token, giving 4 tokens per item. Colliding three-code tuples receive different fourth tokens; non-colliding tuples receive 0. The generator uses 4 x 256 item-token entries.
  - Source: Main RQ levels, codebook cardinality, latent dimension, and collision suffix including zero for a unique tuple: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4. Four position-specific 256-token vocabularies: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p5; one-time collision lookup: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S3.SS1.p8.
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive beam search; numerical beam width not reported. Main evaluation: Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. Cold-start Fig. 5a varies K at epsilon=0.1; Fig. 5b evaluates Recall@10 while varying epsilon. Hardware, inference batch size, and measured latency: not reported.
  - Source: Autoregressive beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A5.p3; main metric cutoffs: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p2; cold-start cutoffs/quota experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.F5. No numerical beam width, inference hardware, inference batch size, or latency is specified after checking Methods/Experiments and Appendices A-E; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p6 give training batches only.
- **Results from**: Original paper Table 1 (main sequential recommendation); Appendix E, Table 9 (three-seed means and standard errors); Fig. 5 (Beauty cold start). Table 1 combines the authors' TIGER results, previously published S3-Rec benchmark results for baselines other than P5, and P5 rerun with modified preprocessing.
  - Source: Original main comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.T1; separate three-seed mean/standard-error table: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A5.T9; cold-start: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.F5. Baselines except P5 were taken from S3-Rec's published results; P5 was rerun with modified preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A4.p2.

### Related

- id: vq-rec; relation: alternative; note: VQ-Rec uses product-quantized content codes for transferable recommendation without generative retrieval; TIGER uses RQ-VAE codes for autoregressive retrieval.; where: TIGER, Section 2, Semantic IDs paragraph: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1; Section 3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S3.SS2.p1.
- id: letter; relation: successor; note: LETTER extends TIGER's semantic-only tokenization with collaborative and diversity regularization, and adds a ranking-guided generation loss.; where: Evidence is from the later LETTER paper, Section 3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p6; Section 4.3.1 explicitly builds the LETTER-TIGER variants: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- id: rpg; relation: alternative; note: RPG predicts long OPQ IDs in parallel and uses graph-constrained decoding, while TIGER generates RQ-VAE IDs autoregressively.; where: Evidence is from the later RPG paper: Section 2 overview, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.p1; Section 2.1.1, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p1; its TIGER baseline description in Section 3.1, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p4.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On Amazon Beauty, TIGER reports Recall@5 of 0.0454 against 0.0387 for SASRec, and RQ-VAE Semantic IDs outperform LSH and random IDs (Tables 1 and 2).
Limitation: The authors state that beam search can make TIGER more expensive than ANN-based retrieval at inference, and the paper does not report a beam width or latency (Appendix E).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Large-scale recommenders usually embed users and items in one space and select candidates by approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search (Abstract). TIGER instead trains a sequence-to-sequence model to decode the Semantic ID (SID) of the next item. The authors describe it as the first Semantic ID-based generative model for recommendation (Abstract). Many later papers in this list keep this pipeline and change one of its stages.

> "We propose a new paradigm of building generative retrieval models for sequential recommendation." (Sec. 1)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```
Item text (title, price, brand, category)
  │
  ▼  pre-trained Sentence-T5
Content embedding x (768 dimensions)
  │
  ▼  DNN encoder, 3-level RQ-VAE, collision token
SID (c1, c2, c3, c4): three codes from 256-entry codebooks plus one collision token
  │
  ▼  Transformer encoder-decoder (T5X), next-token prediction
Next-item SID, decoded by beam search
  │
  ▼  frozen lookup table
Recommended items
```

#### Step 1: Item Text to a Latent Vector

TIGER builds a sentence from each item's title, price, brand, and category, and the pre-trained Sentence-T5 model encodes it into a 768-dimensional embedding $`\mathbf{x}`$ (Sec. 4). A DNN encoder $`E`$ with intermediate layers of size 512, 256, and 128 and ReLU activations maps $`\mathbf{x}`$ to a 32-dimensional latent vector $`\mathbf{z} = E(\mathbf{x})`$ (Sec. 4).

#### Step 2: Residual Quantization into Codes

RQ-VAE quantizes the residual left by the previous level, so each level refines the code of the level before it.

> "Residual-Quantized Variational AutoEncoder (RQ-VAE) [40] is a multi-level vector quantizer that applies quantization on residuals to generate a tuple of codewords (aka Semantic IDs)." (Sec. 3.1)

TIGER uses $`M = 3`$ levels, each with a codebook of $`K = 256`$ codewords of dimension 32 (Sec. 4). At level $`m`$:

```math
\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{z}, \qquad c_m = \arg\min_{k \in \{0, \dots, K-1\}} \left\| \mathbf{r}_m - \mathbf{e}_k^{(m)} \right\|_2^2, \qquad \mathbf{r}_{m+1} = \mathbf{r}_m - \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{r}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{32}`$ is the residual that enters level $`m`$;
- $`\mathbf{e}_k^{(m)}`$ is codeword $`k`$ of the level-$`m`$ codebook;
- $`c_m`$ is the code chosen at level $`m`$.

```python
import torch

def rqvae_quantize(z, codebooks, beta=0.25):
    """
    z:         [B, 32] latent vectors from the encoder E(x)
    codebooks: list of M tensors, each [K, 32] (M = 3, K = 256)
    """
    r = z
    z_hat = torch.zeros_like(z)
    codes, vq_loss = [], 0.0
    for E_m in codebooks:
        # nearest codeword at this level
        c_m = torch.cdist(r, E_m).pow(2).argmin(dim=-1)                     # [B]
        e_m = E_m[c_m]                                                       # [B, 32]
        # codebook and commitment terms of the quantization loss
        vq_loss = vq_loss + (e_m - r.detach()).pow(2).mean() + beta * (r - e_m.detach()).pow(2).mean()
        # straight-through estimate, then the residual for the next level
        z_hat = z_hat + r + (e_m - r).detach()
        r = r - e_m.detach()
        codes.append(c_m)
    return torch.stack(codes, dim=-1), z_hat, vq_loss                        # [B, M], [B, 32], scalar
```

Simplifications: The code shows only the quantization loop and the quantization loss. It omits the DNN encoder and decoder, the reconstruction loss, and the k-means codebook initialization.

#### Step 3: Tokenizer Training

A decoder $`D`$ reconstructs $`\hat{\mathbf{x}} = D(\hat{\mathbf{z}})`$ from the sum of the selected codewords $`\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \sum_{m=1}^{M} \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}`$. RQ-VAE trains the encoder, decoder, and codebooks with a reconstruction loss and a quantization loss:

```math
\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}\|_2^2 + \sum_{m=1}^{M} \left( \left\|\mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{r}_m] - \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}\right\|_2^2 + \beta \left\|\mathbf{r}_m - \mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}]\right\|_2^2 \right)
```

where:
- $`\mathrm{sg}[\cdot]`$ is the stop-gradient operator;
- $`\beta = 0.25`$ weights the commitment term (Sec. 4).

To prevent codebook collapse, TIGER runs k-means on the first training batch and uses the centroids to initialize the codebooks (Sec. 3.1).

#### Step 4: Collision Token

Several items can receive the same three codes. TIGER appends a fourth token so that every item has a unique SID: two items that share (12, 24, 52) become (12, 24, 52, 0) and (12, 24, 52, 1) (Sec. 3.1).

> "To remove the collisions, we append an extra token at the end of the ordered semantic codes to make them unique." (Sec. 3.1)

```python
from collections import defaultdict

def append_collision_token(code_tuples):
    """code_tuples: list of (c1, c2, c3), one per item."""
    seen = defaultdict(int)
    sids = []
    for t in code_tuples:
        sids.append((*t, seen[t]))   # 0 for the first item with this tuple, 1 for the second, ...
        seen[t] += 1
    return sids
```

The code assigns the fourth token in input order; the paper does not state how the order is chosen. The table that maps SIDs to items is built once after the tokenizer is trained and then frozen (Appendix E).

#### Step 5: Sequence-to-Sequence Generation

TIGER flattens a user's history into SID tokens and puts one user token in front. The raw user ID is hashed into one of 2,000 user tokens (Sec. 4). The generator is a Transformer encoder-decoder built with the T5X framework, with 4 layers each in the encoder and the decoder and 6 self-attention heads of dimension 64 (Sec. 4).

> "Given Semantic IDs for items in a user session, a Transformer-based sequence-to-sequence model is trained to predict the Semantic ID of the next item that the user will interact with." (Abstract)

The generator is trained with next-token prediction over the four tokens of the target SID:

```math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{NTP}} = -\sum_{m=1}^{4} \log P_\theta\left(c_{t,m} \mid \mathbf{c}_{1:t-1},\, c_{t,1:m-1}\right)
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{c}_{1:t-1}`$ is the SID token sequence of the history items;
- $`c_{t,m}`$ is the $`m`$-th token of the target item's SID.

At inference, TIGER decodes SIDs with autoregressive beam search and maps each generated SID to an item through the frozen lookup table (Appendix E).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Beauty: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0454, NDCG@5 = 0.0321, Recall@10 = 0.0648, and NDCG@10 = 0.0384, against 0.0387, 0.0249, 0.0605, and 0.0318 for SASRec (Table 1).
- Sports and Outdoors: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0264, NDCG@5 = 0.0181, Recall@10 = 0.0400, and NDCG@10 = 0.0225, against 0.0233, 0.0154, 0.0350, and 0.0192 for SASRec (Table 1).
- Toys and Games: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0521, NDCG@5 = 0.0371, Recall@10 = 0.0712, and NDCG@10 = 0.0432, against 0.0463, 0.0306, 0.0675, and 0.0374 for SASRec (Table 1).
- ID ablation: Table 2 compares random IDs, LSH Semantic IDs, and RQ-VAE Semantic IDs. RQ-VAE IDs score highest and random IDs lowest in all twelve metric columns (Table 2).

  > "Our results show that RQ-VAE consistently outperforms LSH." (Sec. 4.2)

- Invalid IDs: for top-10 predictions, 0.1%–1.6% of generated IDs map to no item across the three datasets (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 6).
- Cold start: the authors state that SIDs improve retrieval of items with no prior interaction history (Abstract, Fig. 5).
- Diversity: temperature-based sampling during decoding controls the diversity of predictions (Sec. 4.3).
- ID length and codebook size: the authors also tried other settings, such as 6 codewords from codebooks of size 64.

  > "We noticed that the recommendation metrics for TIGER were robust to these changes." (Appendix E)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The authors state that TIGER can be more expensive than ANN-based models at inference because of beam search (Appendix E).

> "we note that our model can be more computationally expensive than ANN-based models during inference due to the use of beam search for autoregressive decoding." (Appendix E)

**Our analysis.**

- TIGER's representation uses item text only (`Text`). LETTER uses text and collaborative signals (`Text+CF`) with a learnable RQ tokenizer (`Learn. RQ`).
- The tokenizer is fixed before the generator trains (`Fixed`). ETEGRec updates the tokenizer and the generator in turns (`Altern.`).
- The fourth token only separates items that share three codes; the paper derives it from the collision, not from item content (Sec. 3.1).
- Unconstrained beam search can produce IDs that map to no item (Sec. 4.5). LETTER decodes with constrained beam search (`C-Beam`).
- Beam search runs one generator step per SID token. RPG predicts all tokens of an SID in parallel (`Non-AR`) and decodes over a graph of valid IDs (`Graph`).

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/tokenrec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### TokenRec：面向 LLM 生成推荐的 ID 分词

> TokenRec 用掩码向量量化 tokenizer 将用户和物品 ID 转为多 token 表示，增强 LLM 对协同结构的建模能力。

### 研究动机与问题定义

原子 ID 缺乏语义且词表规模随物品数增长，多 token 表示又需要合理分配协同信息。TokenRec 学习 LLM 兼容的 ID tokenization，用于推荐表示与检索。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`交互图与ID → 多码本量化 → 用户/物品 token → 序列编码 → 全物品评分`

方法用 K-way encoder 和掩码向量量化器学习物品 token，并用 K-to-1 decoder 重构原始表示；用户也可通过 MQ-tokenizer 表示。T5-small 编码用户表示，再与 GNN 物品表示计算余弦相似度，对全物品排序并取 Top-K。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户-物品交互与高阶协同结构 |
| 信息融入位置 | 向量数据库、tokenizer 和生成输入 |
| 语义标识结构 | K 个离散 token 的序列 |
| 适用场景 | LLM 生成式推荐与新物品泛化 |

### 方法设计

#### 2-A 记号与整体框架
TokenRec 将用户和物品表示为可组合的多 token code。用户 tokenizer 可将用户协同表示转成兼容 token；推荐模型使用这些表示完成检索。

#### 2-B 掩码向量量化 tokenizer
K-way encoder 为一个物品生成多个潜向量，掩码向量量化器从多个 codebook 中选择离散 token。K-to-1 decoder 重构原始表示，使不同 code 的组合仍保留协同信息，并通过高阶交互增强区分度。

#### 2-C 推荐检索
LLM（T5-small）编码用户表示，再与 GNN 物品表示计算余弦相似度，对全部物品排序取 Top-K，不逐码生成 SID（§II-D.3，p6，Eq. 17–19；§II-E.2，p7）。当前记录为 Encoder、Discrim.、Scoring。

#### 2-D 效率与泛化
论文分析新用户/物品、codebook 规模、效率和消融，重点说明多 token 表示相对原子 ID 的词表与泛化优势。

### 实验结论

- TokenRec 在多个数据集上改善了推荐效果。
- 多码本 tokenizer 带来更好的效率与泛化能力。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 向量数据库与多码本维护增加工程依赖。
- 动态用户/物品更新和大规模在线延迟仍需更多验证。

#### 研究定位
TokenRec 的贡献是把协同 ID 学习为可组合 token，适合放在“LLM 物品分词与协同表示”章节。

### 标签

`多码本量化` · `ID分词` · `LLM推荐` · `生成式检索`

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/vstar.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### V-STAR：价值引导结构化采样与优化

> V-STAR 让生成式推荐把搜索预算集中到高价值分支，并联合学习价值模型与结构化解码策略。

### 研究动机与问题定义

束搜索会在大量低价值分支上浪费计算，单纯扩大搜索预算也未必改善推荐。V-STAR 研究如何使用价值估计选择值得继续探索的 SID 前缀。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史 → SID前缀搜索 → 价值模型 → 结构化采样 → 完整SID → 推荐物品`

方法学习估计候选前缀价值的模型，提出 Value-Guided Efficient Decoding 选择搜索分支，并用 Sibling-GRPO 让策略从同层兄弟候选的相对价值中学习。生成完整 SID 后直接得到物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户历史、SID 前缀概率和候选价值 |
| 信息融入位置 | 价值模型、解码选择和策略训练 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化序列 |
| 适用场景 | 搜索预算受限的生成式推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 语义感知价值模型
V-STAR 学习估计 SID 前缀在当前用户上下文下的推荐价值。价值模型同时参考生成概率、语义/协同表示和候选结果质量，为搜索过程提供比局部 token 概率更长程的判断。

#### 4.2 价值引导高效解码
VED 在树状 SID 空间中优先扩展高价值前缀，将有限搜索预算集中到更有希望的分支。它保留结构化约束，避免生成无法映射到物品的标识。

#### 4.3 Sibling-GRPO
Sibling-GRPO 将同一父节点下的兄弟候选组成相对比较组，用组内优势更新生成策略。这样模型能学习在局部结构中选择真正有价值的分支。

#### 4.4 训练与测试
V-STAR 形成解码-学习自演化闭环：解码器提供候选，价值模型评价候选，策略优化再改善解码。实验比较搜索预算、离线指标、线上效果和消融。

### 实验结论

- 价值引导解码在相同搜索预算下优于普通束搜索。
- 价值模型与策略优化具有互补作用。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 额外价值模型和采样逻辑增加系统复杂度。
- 价值估计误差可能导致高价值分支被错误剪枝。

#### 研究定位
V-STAR 的主要贡献是按候选价值分配生成搜索预算，适合放在“高效解码与搜索优化”章节。

### 标签

`价值引导解码` · `结构化采样` · `GRPO` · `生成式推荐`

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/vqrec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### VQ-Rec：可迁移序列推荐的向量量化物品表示

> VQ-Rec 将物品文本编码为离散 code，再查表获得序列推荐器的物品表示，以提升跨域迁移能力。

### 研究动机与问题定义

传统物品 ID 与具体物品绑定，难以跨域迁移；直接使用文本又会让推荐器表示不稳定。VQ-Rec 关注的是可迁移的物品表示学习，而不是生成式检索。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品文本 → PLM表示 → 产品量化code → code embedding → 序列编码器评分`

模型用固定 PLM 编码物品文本，再通过优化产品量化得到离散 code，并查表聚合为物品向量。推荐器使用该向量进行对比预训练和跨域微调，最终通过全物品评分排序，而非生成完整 SID。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 物品文本、用户交互和跨域数据 |
| 信息融入位置 | 物品表示和序列编码器输入 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多维离散 code 向量 |
| 适用场景 | 可迁移序列推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 2.1 向量量化物品表示
VQ-Rec 先用固定 BERT/PLM 把物品文本编码为向量，再用优化产品量化将向量拆分成多个离散 code。每个 code 维度有独立 codebook，多个 code 的 embedding 查表后平均得到物品表示。

#### 2.2 对比式推荐器预训练
模型构造真实下一物品、半合成负样本和混合域负样本，训练序列编码器区分它们。code embedding 表在该阶段学习，使离散表示能承载可迁移协同关系。

#### 2.3 跨域推荐器微调
迁移到目标域时，论文分别微调 code 与序列推荐器。文本到 code 的映射可在新物品上重新分配，推荐器则使用共享 code embedding 适应目标域。

#### 2.4 讨论与范围
VQ-Rec 最终通过序列编码器对物品进行全物品评分，而不是自回归生成完整 SID。因此它是语义/量化表示学习相关方法。

### 实验结论

- 量化 code 表示改善了跨域序列推荐和冷启动物品表现。
- 对比预训练与跨域微调均有作用。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 不属于直接生成完整 SID 的生成式推荐方法。
- 全物品评分需要维护物品表示并进行候选计算。

#### 研究定位
VQ-Rec 适合放在“语义标识生成式推荐的前置表示学习与相关工作”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.12316)

### 检索方式补充

迁自 `d61aa6c:tables/boundary-and-excluded-methods.md` 的机制说明。

量化 code 仅作为序列推荐器表示，最终依赖全物品评分。

旧表的“核心／边界／排除”分组已由当前问题与阶段分类取代。
